categories.name: Bookkeeping
categories.description: Keeping records in order through the year.

categories.name: Tax dates
categories.description: The filing year and how to meet it calmly.

posts.title: A shoebox is not a system
posts.excerpt: Three folders and ten minutes a week keep a sole trader’s receipts ready for the return.
posts.content:
One folder for income, one for costs, one for anything you are not sure about. That is the whole system.

Ten minutes every Friday is enough to keep it. In January, the third folder is the only one we need to talk about.

posts.title: When to become a company
posts.excerpt: Profit level, liability and paperwork: three questions to ask before you incorporate.
posts.content:
Incorporating can lower the tax on a growing profit, but it brings payroll, annual accounts and a second return.

We usually suggest waiting until profit is steady for two years. Bring both years to a first hour and we will run the numbers.

posts.title: The year-end adjustment, explained
posts.excerpt: What the December paperwork is for, and why staff should hand it in early.
posts.content:
Through the year, payroll withholds tax on an estimate. In December the estimate is corrected, and most staff see a small refund.

The papers we ask for in early December make that correction possible. Late papers mean a separate return in March.

posts.title: A calm February
posts.excerpt: How we plan the busiest month so that nobody, including us, files at midnight.
posts.content:
We ask for papers in January and set every client a week in February. The return is filed in that week.

By March the office is quiet again, and refunds have mostly arrived.

posts.title: Records to keep, and for how long
posts.excerpt: Seven years for most records; a short list of what belongs in the box.
posts.content:
Keep invoices, receipts, bank statements and contracts for seven years from the filing date.

Landlords should also keep purchase papers for the property for as long as they own it, and then seven years more.

posts.title: Payroll for your first employee
posts.excerpt: Enrolment, payslips and withholding: the first month with a team of two.
posts.content:
Before the first payday, register as an employer and enrol your employee in social insurance.

From then on payroll is a monthly rhythm: payslips on the same day, withholding paid by the tenth of the next month.
